title: Core Governance Rewards are already flowing while the compliance standards that gate eligibility remain unwritten
content:
A.2.2.11.1.2 conditions the reward on compliance: "the frontend maintained by the Integrator must satisfy compliance requirements as specified in A.2.2.11.1.3." Following that reference, A.2.2.11.1.3.1 states that "Specific security standards for compliant frontends will be specified in a future iteration of the Atlas," and A.2.2.11.1.3.2 says the same of information and disclosure standards.

Meanwhile the Primitive is live. A.2.2.11.1.2.1 names Skybase as a current eligible recipient for the sky.money frontend, A.2.2.11.1.4.1 makes distributions monthly through the Treasury Management Function, and A.2.2.11.1.5 backdates allocations "retroactive to May 19, 2025," with accrued amounts funded from the Core Council Buffer.

The eligibility test is therefore vacuous at present: the gate is defined by reference to a document that does not yet contain a standard, so "compliant" currently means "listed." For a Primitive whose stated purpose is ensuring Governance Security is *maintained over time*, the quality bar is the entire substance — payment without it buys the existence of a frontend rather than its security.

This is a recognisable Atlas pattern: commit the structure and funding first, defer the specifics. It is defensible while the recipient list has one entry vetted by other means, and it degrades as the list grows, because each addition sets precedent in the absence of a written test. Worth tracking as an open gap rather than reading the compliance clause as an active control.
description: Eligibility requires a frontend to satisfy compliance requirements, yet both the security and information standards are deferred to a future Atlas iteration
